ap_biology-f01.title: Interpreting and evaluating results: cultured cells

stimulus.description: A researcher investigates how a growth factor affects cell division in cultured cells. Cells were grown with four concentrations of the growth factor, and the percent of cells in mitosis was determined after 24 hours. Each treatment was repeated n = 8 times. Mean percent of cells in mitosis (percent of cells) ± 2SE for cultured cells at four levels of the independent variable; n = 8 for each level

columns: Mean percent of cells in mitosis (percent of cells) ± 2SE

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe how binding of a growth factor to a receptor on a cell can lead to cell division.
parts.model_answer: The growth factor binds to a receptor, which starts a signal transduction pathway of relay proteins that results in a cellular response such as activating genes needed for division.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct explanation or description of the biological concept
required_elements: Binding of the growth factor to the receptor starts a signal transduction pathway that results in a cell response
alt_solutions: the receptor relays the signal through a series of proteins to turn on division
the signal received at the receptor is transduced into activation of genes for division
common_errors: says the growth factor enters the nucleus and directly copies DNA
describes only the binding without any resulting pathway or response
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: (i) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in the investigation. (ii) Identify one factor that should be kept constant so the results are due to the independent variable. (iii) Describe the pattern in the data in the table.
parts.model_answer: (i) Independent variable: concentration of the growth factor; dependent variable: percent of cells in mitosis. (ii) For example temperature. (iii) The mean percent of cells in mitosis increases as the independent variable increases, from 4.0 to 17.1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies both the independent variable and the dependent variable
required_elements: The independent variable is concentration of the growth factor and the dependent variable is percent of cells in mitosis
alt_solutions: manipulated variable: concentration of the growth factor; measured response: percent of cells in mitosis
changes concentration of the growth factor and measures percent of cells in mitosis
common_errors: names the dependent variable as the independent variable
names only one of the two variables
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a valid factor that is kept constant
required_elements: Names a factor other than the independent variable that is held the same in all treatments
alt_solutions: temperature
the number of cells plated
the incubation time
common_errors: names the independent variable as the constant
names a factor that was changed between treatments
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the pattern in the data, using values from the table
required_elements: States that the mean percent of cells in mitosis increases as the independent variable increases, citing values
alt_solutions: the percent of cells in mitosis goes up from 4.0 to 17.1
the values increase across the levels, citing the first and last means
common_errors: describes the opposite trend
describes the pattern without any values from the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: (i) Calculate the percent change in the mean percent of cells in mitosis from the lowest level to the highest level of the independent variable. Show your work. (ii) Using the ±2SE values, determine whether the difference between the mean at 5 and the mean at 10 is statistically supported, and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: (i) percent change = (17.1 - 4.0) / 4.0 x 100 = 327.5%. (ii) 5: 8.14 to 10.06; 10: 12.64 to 14.56. The ranges do not overlap, so the difference between the two treatments is statistically supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up the percent change with the correct formula and values (expression)
required_elements: Uses (final - initial) / initial x 100 with the values 17.1 and 4.0
alt_solutions: percent change = difference divided by the starting value times 100
common_errors: divides by the final value instead of the initial value
forgets to multiply by 100
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct percent change (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: States whether the difference is supported and justifies it by comparing the ±2SE ranges

separated error ranges mean the difference is unlikely to be due to chance
common_errors: compares only the means
states the wrong conclusion for the ranges
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Predict how the percent of cells in mitosis at 20 ng/mL would change if a drug that blocks the growth factor receptor were added, and justify your prediction.

predicts that all cells would stop dividing permanently
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the prediction with biological reasoning

says the cells lose their DNA
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.
